answer: Bind each identity to its own cross-epoch commitment chain: every answer hashes the previous one, and the beacon accepts a new claim only if the prior hash in that chain verifies, so each identity must maintain an unbroken, verifiable line across many epochs. A haven for clones collapses because a fleet of k identities must publish k separate chains, each rooted in real prior work; the cost per clone grows with every epoch the chain runs. The system checks a lotus of nested proofs at draw time, and any gap in the oasis of hashes voids the claim before it earns.
